json.objectWhy: A small tool you use every day: add, tick off, and watch a streak grow.

steps.does: Write index.html: the shell of the habit app in plain HTML. A header with the app name, a form with a text input and a button to add a habit, an empty unordered list where habits will be shown, a section where the streak summary appears, and a footer. Each habit row will later carry a tick control for today and a delete control; leave empty list items to be filled by app.js. Load styles.css in the head and app.js at the end of the body. No frameworks, no build step, no files other than the three written here.
done: styles.css and app.js are the only files it loads

files.purpose: page shell: add-habit form, habit list, streak summary, footer

steps.focus: One page, three files, nothing else.
steps.title: Build page

steps.does: Write styles.css for the page made in step 1. Use only the selectors already present in index.html. Plain CSS with CSS variables for colours, a readable layout that works on a narrow phone screen and a desktop, a clear ticked versus unticked state for a habit, and buttons that look pressable. Any icon or decorative graphic must be drawn with CSS or inline SVG, since no image files are allowed.
done: every selector used matches an element written in index.html

files.purpose: layout and styling for the habit page

steps.title: Style the app

steps.does: Write app.js against the elements in index.html. Keep the list of habits in localStorage under one key, with each habit holding a name, a created date, and the dates it was ticked. Render the list from that stored data on load. Wire the add-habit form to create a habit, the tick control to toggle today's date on a habit, and a delete control to remove it. Compute the current streak for each habit from the stored dates and show it next to the habit and in the summary section. Handle the empty case with a short message and guard against malformed stored data.
done: no framework or library is used
adding, ticking, deleting and reloading all work from stored data

files.purpose: habit state, localStorage, ticking and streak maths

steps.focus: The state lives in localStorage; the page is only a view of it.
steps.title: Add app logic

steps.does: Read index.html, styles.css and app.js as a critical colleague. List what is weak or missing: unclear streak behaviour, habits that could be lost, a control that is hard to reach on a phone, missing empty state, anything a first-time user would find confusing. Write the list as short points naming the file and the element involved. Do not rewrite the files here.
done: each point names a file and the element or function it concerns
steps.focus: Find the weak spots before the code check does.
steps.title: Second reader

steps.does: Check the finished app by code: index.html and styles.css parse, app.js loads without a syntax error, the page loads only styles.css and app.js, every CSS selector used matches an element written in index.html, and each required part of the page is present. Report anything that fails with the file and line it came from.
done: any failure is reported with its file
steps.focus: Only what can be checked by machine.

required.what: text input for a new habit name and a button to add it
the list of habits, each row with a tick control and a delete control
the per-habit streak counts and an overall summary
the app name and a one-line description of what it does
a short note that habits are kept in this browser's local storage

steps.title: Run the check

json.summary: Page shell for the habit tracker: header with the app name and a light/dark theme switch, add-habit form (labelled text input plus submit button), an empty habit list, a streaks summary, and a footer. Loads styles.css in the head and app.js with defer at the end of the body; no other assets, no inline styles or scripts, no inline event handlers. The theme switch is a button (#theme-toggle) with aria-pressed for the dark state and two inline icons (sun and moon) that the CSS shows one at a time from the data-theme attribute on <html>; the shell ships with data-theme="light" as the default, and every class and id from the previous version is kept exactly as it was so app.js and styles.css keep working. index.html alone cannot switch the theme or remember it, because the rules for this page allow no inline script and no extra files: app.js as it stands has no handler for #theme-toggle, so it needs a small addition that reads the saved value at start-up, sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme to "light" or "dark", keeps aria-pressed and the button's accessible name in step, and writes the choice back to local storage under its own key; styles.css then needs the dark palette under html[data-theme="dark"] plus a matching color-scheme declaration so form controls and scrollbars follow the theme. Until those two additions land, the button is present and reachable but does nothing when pressed, and the page stays light. Nothing else about the page changed.
app.js storing habits and theme in localStorage, with add/tick/delete wiring, streak maths, a guarded parser for stored data, and the light/dark switch kept in step
Rewrote styles.css so the light/dark switch is styled and driven by data-theme on <html>, keeping every earlier rule for the page, the habit items and the summary.

issues.text: app.js — loadHabits() and saveHabits(): if the stored value is corrupt, unreadable or blocked, loadHabits() hands back an empty list and the very next save overwrites the old value. The person sees an empty tracker and no message at all, and the lost habits are not kept anywhere as a backup.

app.js — saveHabits(): the catch block swallows quota and blocked-storage errors. Habits keep appearing in the list for the rest of the session, so nothing on screen says saving failed; they are simply gone after a reload.

app.js — deleteHabit(): deleting is immediate, with no confirmation and no undo. In styles.css the .delete-btn sits in .habit-actions right beside the tick button, so one mis-tap removes a habit and its whole tick history.

app.js — toggleTick() only ever uses todayKey(), so a day the person missed can never be ticked in afterwards; one forgotten day caps the streak for good. In the same .habit-item the two labels disagree: .habit-meta reads 'Not ticked yet' while .habit-streak reads '1 day streak', because currentStreak() still counts a tick from yesterday and nothing on the page explains that rule.

app.js — render() and #summary-streak: 'best' is the highest current streak, not the best ever, so a habit with a long run that ended last month contributes 0 and the summary reads '0 days'. A first-time user reading that tile will think the app forgot their record.

app.js — loadTheme() and applyTheme(): there is no prefers-color-scheme fallback, so someone whose system is dark gets a light page on the first visit and has to find the switch (the .theme-toggle in the header). applyTheme() also only sets data-theme on <html>, so nothing updates a theme-color meta for the browser bar.

app.js — onStorage(): a theme key that is removed in another tab goes through validTheme(null), which returns 'light' and forces light mode rather than falling back to the page default; event.key === null (a localStorage.clear() in another tab) is not handled at all, so the other tab keeps showing stale habits.

app.js — addHabit(): there is no duplicate check, so the same habit typed twice makes two rows with separate streaks. Names longer than MAX_NAME_LENGTH are cut silently with no hint, and a blank or whitespace-only submit is rejected with no message — the field just keeps the text and gets focus.

styles.css — @media (max-width: 34rem) turns .habit-item into a column (flex-direction: column) and stretches .habit-side, roughly doubling the height of every row on a phone, so a list of habits needs a lot of scrolling. The .btn-quiet .delete-btn shows only a trash icon, and on a touch screen there is no hover to reveal what it does.

redos.instruction: Add a light and dark theme switch, and remember the choice.
